info.title: Hopscotch
info.description:
An OpenAI-compatible inference API. Point an OpenAI client at https://api.hopscotchlabs.ai, give it a Hopscotch API key, and call models across providers on one prepaid balance.

Every response, errors included, matches the shape an unmodified OpenAI SDK expects.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. Vertex Gemini forwards this as generationConfig.temperature; Gemini 3.8 Flash ignores custom sampling values. Invalid values may still be rejected by Google. Omit this control on that model.

top_p.description: Sampling probability. Vertex Gemini forwards this as generationConfig.topP; Gemini 3.8 Flash ignores custom sampling values. Invalid values may still be rejected by Google.

top_k.description: Sampling candidate count. Vertex Gemini forwards this as generationConfig.topK; Gemini 3.8 Flash ignores custom sampling values. Invalid values may still be rejected by Google.

presence_penalty.description: Vertex Gemini forwards every non-null value unchanged as generationConfig.presencePenalty, including zero and nonzero values on Gemini 3.8 Flash and its preview variants. Google validates values and model-specific support; the adapter does not reject penalties by model. Null is omitted. Google's parameter refusals retain their HTTP status and readable reason in the OpenAI error envelope. A successful response does not guarantee that the model uses the parameter.

frequency_penalty.description: Vertex Gemini forwards every non-null value unchanged as generationConfig.frequencyPenalty, including zero and nonzero values on Gemini 3.8 Flash and its preview variants. Google validates values and model-specific support; the adapter does not reject penalties by model. Null is omitted. Google's parameter refusals retain their HTTP status and readable reason in the OpenAI error envelope. A successful response does not guarantee that the model uses the parameter.

safety_settings.description: Vertex Gemini safety settings. safetySettings is an equivalent alias. Send one spelling. If both are supplied, equal JSON values are accepted (object key order is ignored; array order is significant); different values return 400 with a message naming both fields. The platform-credential error boundary clears param and code. An explicit null is forwarded as null and is not treated as omission.

safetySettings.description: Alias of safety_settings for Vertex Gemini. Equal values supplied under both names are accepted; conflicting values return 400 with a message naming both fields. The platform-credential error boundary clears param and code. OFF is forwarded unchanged.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning control interpreted by the selected provider. Vertex Gemini 3.8 Flash maps low, medium or high to its thinking level; minimal is unsupported. Other providers retain their own supported values. Empty or whitespace-only strings return 400 with code invalid_value and param reasoning_effort. Gemini also rejects 0 and false.

model.description: The exact provider-qualified ID returned by GET /v1/models, for example vertex-ai/gemini-3.8-flash. The offering must include chat_completions in endpoint_families. A bare ID is refused with model_id_not_pinned. A profile/{identifier} value selects your routing profile instead.

max_tokens.description: The most output tokens the reply may use. Optional, as it is on OpenAI. Left out, it is filled in for the providers whose own API refuses a request that does not carry one, and the figure used is the model's published max_output_tokens, which GET /v1/models/{model} reports and which is what credit is held for on a request naming no ceiling. Every other provider is sent the request unchanged. max_completion_tokens counts as this field being given.

200.description:
A chat completion. For a direct nonstreamed request, model names the requested public ID. Gemini can return text in message.content and generated images in message.images as image_url data URLs.

With stream: true, read text/event-stream data frames through data: [DONE]. Gemini image output is carried in choices[].delta.images. Set stream_options.include_usage for a final usage chunk. A successful HTTP status alone does not guarantee visible text or an image: check content and finish_reason. Thinking usage can be recorded when no visible completion is returned.

x-hopscotch-served-by.description: The full id, "{provider}/{model}", of the model that actually answered: the pinned id when the request named one directly, or the routing-profile chain member that served when the request named a profile.

x-hopscotch-served-via.description: Present as backup when a backup route served this request. Absent on ordinary direct responses. Read x-hopscotch-provider with x-hopscotch-served-by when checking which model served.

x-hopscotch-cache-status.description: What the response cache did for this request: HIT served an exact-match stored entry with no provider call, HIT:semantic served a near-duplicate stored entry for a separately opted-in workspace on chat completions with no provider call, MISS served the provider and stored the reply where eligible, and BYPASS with a reason sat the cache out (not_opted_in, skip, model_ineligible, provider_ineligible, model_unknown, model_unreadable, nondeterministic, zdr, ttl_unreadable, an unservable reply class, and the rest). Absent while the response cache flag is off, where the reply reads exactly as before the cache.

400.description: The request cannot be served as sent. `code` is null for a missing parameter, with `param` naming it, `context_length_exceeded` for a request too large to price or serve in one call, and `provider_key_refused` when the request ran on your own key for a provider that rejected it or refused this particular call under it. On the platform's own provider keys this route also refuses, with `code` null and `param` naming the field and never its value, a field that buys something this platform cannot bill yet or keeps the conversation at the provider: a `service_tier` other than `auto`, `default` or `on_demand`, `web_search_options`, a hosted tool the provider charges for per call, audio output or an input-audio shape the selected route cannot meter, a `cache_control` marker with a `1h` ttl, and `store: true`. A request served on your own provider key keeps every one of them. See Request parameters.

error.message: You must provide a model parameter naming the model to call. It is read to work out what the request could cost before it is sent.

context_length_exceeded.summary: Too large to serve in one call

error.message: This request is too large to price: it is estimated at 4000000 prompt tokens, which is beyond anything this platform can hold credit for. Send less in one call.

provider_key_refused.summary: Your own provider key was rejected

error.message: openai rejected your workspace's own openai key (401), so the credential itself was not accepted. Replace it on the Provider keys screen. While your workspace holds a key for openai, every request to openai runs on yours and none is sent on a Hopscotch key, so no other credential was tried for it. Nothing was charged for this request. Remove the key on the Provider keys screen and these requests go back to running on Hopscotch's key and being charged for.

401.description:
No key, a scheme other than Bearer, a key of the wrong shape, or a key we reject. An unknown key and a revoked key are answered with one identical message on purpose.

A key past its own expiry date is refused here too, with code `key_expired` and a message naming the date. It is checked before the per-minute rate limiter, so an expired key never consumes that allowance. Expired keys are not renewed: create a new one.

error.message: Incorrect API key provided.

402.description: The request will not be paid for, and nothing was charged. Code `insufficient_credit` is the workspace being out of credit, which stops every key on it. Code `key_limit_exceeded` is the sending key reaching its own credit limit, which leaves every other key in the workspace serving normally; it is refused before any credit is held, and the message names what that key has settled and holds inside its current window.

insufficient_credit.summary: The workspace is out of credit

error.message: This account has 54 minor units available and the request needs 55 held.

key_limit_exceeded.summary: This key is at its own limit

error.message: This key may spend $20.00 in its current window and has $18.40 settled and $1.70 held against that, so a request needing $0.30 more is refused. Nothing was charged for it and no credit was held. The limit belongs to this key alone, so other keys in the workspace are unaffected. This limit resets monthly on UTC calendar windows, so requests are admitted again when the window rolls. It can also be raised or removed on the Keys screen.

403.description: Refused for a setting the caller owns rather than anything about the model, and `code` names which. A key whose account staff have suspended is refused with code `account_suspended`, before any credit is held or any provider is called; contact support, because retrying will not change the answer.

error.message: This account is suspended, so it cannot send requests. Contact support. Request id REQUEST_ID.

404.description: The model cannot be served, and the two cases are told apart by `code`. `model_not_found` means the id is in no catalog at all, which is what a typo produces, so check the spelling or list what this key can call with `GET /v1/models`. `model_not_available` means the id is catalogued and is not being served right now, either on this endpoint or at all, so retrying later is worth more than changing the request. No provider was called either way.

model_not_found.summary: No model of that id exists

error.message: The model "MODEL_ID" does not exist. Check the spelling, or list the models this key can call with GET /v1/models.

model_not_available.summary: Known to us, and not being served right now

error.message: The model "MODEL_ID" is not currently available. It is known to this platform and is not being served right now, so retrying later is worth more than changing the request.

model_not_available_endpoint.summary: Live, and not offered on this endpoint

error.message: "MODEL_ID" is not offered on this endpoint: the catalog lists it for chat and not for embeddings.

409.description: Reserved for workload insights, which is not available yet. A request that does not name a workflow never receives it.

413.description: The request body is larger than the 8388608 byte maximum this API accepts, so it was refused at the door. A body that declares its length is refused without a byte being read; one that declares none is read only as far as the ceiling and then abandoned. Nothing was parsed, no credit was held, no model was called and nothing was charged.

payload_too_large.summary: The request body is over the ceiling

error.message: This request body is larger than the 8388608 byte maximum this API accepts. Nothing was read, no model was called and nothing was charged. Send fewer messages, a shorter prompt, or fewer inputs.

429.description: A limit refused the request. `rate_limit_exceeded` is this key's own request rate and carries `Retry-After`. `spend_rate_exceeded` is the account spend rate cap, which counts the credit held for requests rather than the credit they settle at; send `max_tokens` to hold less. `provider_key_refused` is your own key for a provider being over its limit there; it clears on its own and carries no `Retry-After`. `upstream_rate_limited` is the model's provider rate-limiting the call: nothing about the request is wrong, nothing is charged, and it carries `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. Present on `rate_limit_exceeded` and on `upstream_rate_limited`.

error.message: Rate limit reached for this key. Try again in 12 seconds. Request id REQUEST_ID.

This account has already reserved 5000 minor units in the last 60 seconds, which is at its ceiling of 5000. Requests are admitted again within 60 seconds of the earliest reservation counted, with nothing to do in the meantime.

provider_key_refused.summary: Your own provider key is over its limit

error.message: openai refused this request as over its limits, on your workspace's own openai key. This is your account's limit at openai rather than ours. While your workspace holds a key for openai, every request to openai runs on yours and none is sent on a Hopscotch key, so no other credential was tried for it. Nothing was charged for this request. Remove the key on the Provider keys screen and these requests go back to running on Hopscotch's key and being charged for.

upstream_rate_limited.summary: The model's provider rate-limited the call

error.message: The provider serving this model is rate-limiting requests right now. Nothing was charged. Retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header. Quote the request id if you contact support.

500.description: A fault on our side. The request id is the one thing worth keeping.

error.message: The server had an error while processing your request. Sorry about that! Quote the request id if you contact support.

503.description: Ours rather than yours, and `code` names the condition. `paused_by_owner` clears only when somebody lifts the pause, so retrying on a timer will not help. `balance_unavailable` (we could not read the balance, so the request was refused rather than served unmetered), `model_not_priceable` and `model_pricing_unreadable` (a model we list could not be priced for this call) and `no_provider_configured` (we are not currently configured to serve this) all clear without you doing anything. An offering without usable published prices can return model_pricing_unreadable before a provider call or charge.

error.message: Every request on this account is paused, because somebody with access to it pressed Pause in the dashboard. Nothing was charged for this request and no credit was held for it. It is retryable, and it will be refused the same way until the pause is lifted, so retrying on a timer will not clear it. Requests start working again the moment the pause is lifted from the same control, with nothing else to do and nothing to re-create.

balance_unavailable.summary: We could not read the balance

error.message: Your credit balance could not be checked while this request was running, so it was stopped rather than left unwatched. This is a fault on our side rather than a problem with your account, and it does not mean you are out of credit. Try again shortly.

504.description: The request ran past the request deadline and was terminated.

error.message: This request ran longer than the 540 second limit and was terminated. Reduce the amount of work in one call, or stream the response, and try again.

529.description: The model's provider answered `529` rather than `429`. Carries the same `upstream_rate_limited` code as the 429 case, with `type` `api_error` as the status class requires: nothing about the request is wrong, nothing is charged, and it carries `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. Present the same way as on the 429 `upstream_rate_limited`.

upstream_rate_limited.summary: The model's provider rate-limited the call, at 529

error.message: The provider serving this model is rate-limiting requests right now. Nothing was charged. Retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header. Quote the request id if you contact support.

post.description:
Send an OpenAI-compatible chat request. Set stream: true for server-sent events. Select an exact model ID from GET /v1/models and check endpoint_families. Offered Vertex Gemini image models can generate images when modalities includes image.

Credit is held at admission and settled using published customer rates and recorded usage. Read the settled charge with GET /v1/usage/{id}, using the x-hopscotch-request-id response header.

model.description: A model id in `provider/model` form, or `profile/{identifier}` for one of your workspace's routing profiles. A bare model id is refused with 400 and the code `model_id_not_pinned`. The catalog must list the model for completions. List what you can call with GET /v1/models.

prompt.description: What to complete: a string, an array of strings, an array of token ids, or an array of token id arrays.

stream.description: Return the reply as server-sent events instead of one JSON body.

max_tokens.description: The most output tokens you will accept. Sending it also lowers the credit held for the request while it runs. Omit it and the model's published maximum output is held instead.

schema.description: An OpenAI text completion request. Fields beyond the ones named here are forwarded to the provider unchanged rather than refused for being unfamiliar.

200.description:
The completion, in OpenAI's text completion format as the provider produced it. A response that is not streamed carries the provider's token counts in its own `usage` object.

When `stream` is true the body is `text/event-stream` instead, in OpenAI's own chunk format, ending with `data: [DONE]`.

Absent on every other response, and never sent with any other value, so a client that has never read it sees nothing change about an ordinary request. The provider named on x-hopscotch-provider and in the body is still the one you asked for.

post.description:
Send an OpenAI text completion request, the older format that takes a `prompt` rather than `messages`. Set `stream: true` for server-sent events.

The body is forwarded as you sent it, so a field this page does not name still reaches the provider, and the reply is the provider's text completion object.

On the platform's own provider keys this route applies the same refusals as chat completions. See the 400 response. A request served on your own provider key keeps every one of those fields.

Credit is held when the request is admitted and settled against the provider's own token counts when it finishes. You are charged the provider's rate at face value. Nothing is added per request.

To read back the tokens and charge of one request afterwards, send the value of the `x-hopscotch-request-id` response header to `GET /v1/usage/{id}`.

get.description:
List the models you can call. The `id` of each entry is what you send as `model`.

Each entry is the OpenAI model object with a `uniblock` block beside it, carrying what OpenAI's own object has no field for: who serves the model, what it can do, its context window, and the provider's list price.

post.description:
Send a request in the Anthropic Messages format. Set `stream: true` for Anthropic's own server-sent event stream.

The credential is read from either `Authorization: Bearer` or Anthropic's own `x-api-key` header, so an unmodified Anthropic SDK works whichever way it authenticates. If both headers are present they must carry the same key: two different keys are refused with 401 rather than one being chosen.

`max_tokens` is required by Anthropic and is passed through as you send it. It is not defaulted here, and a request that leaves it out is refused by the provider in the provider's own words. It is also the figure the credit held for the request is sized from. An `anthropic-version` header is not forwarded.

This route differs from Anthropic's own API in one way: a refusal comes back in the OpenAI error envelope that every other route here uses, so an Anthropic SDK reads the sentence from `error.message`. Only `POST /v1/messages` is served. `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` is not, and answers 404 with the code `endpoint_not_supported`.

Credit is held when the request is admitted and settled against the provider's own token counts when it finishes. You are charged the provider's rate at face value. Nothing is added per request.

To read back the tokens and charge of one request afterwards, send the value of the `x-hopscotch-request-id` response header to `GET /v1/usage/{id}`.

post.description: Create a video job, in OpenAI's Sora shape (`client.videos.create`), and answer the provider's job object. A hold of `seconds` (4 when absent) times the model's per-second rate for the requested `size` is taken before anything is sent to the provider, and stays open until the job ends: a completed job is charged the seconds the provider reports, never above the hold; a failed or provider-confirmed cancelled job is charged nothing; a job not finished three hours after create is charged its full hold. One usage row is written per job, when it settles. The hold is zero on a workspace-owned credential. A model whose rates are duration tiers holds the requested seconds at the tier equal to them, and at the dearest tier when the seconds name none, so a hold never undercharges. A completed job reporting zero seconds releases the hold and records served usage at zero charge; absent or unreadable seconds charge the full hold. Video usage is timestamped when the job settles, so its usage period follows the settled charge. The body may be JSON or multipart/form-data (an `input_reference` image rides in the form) and is capped at 8 MiB; a larger body is refused 413 before any hold. The job belongs to the account that created it: the follow-up paths answer only that account. Listing (`GET /v1/videos`) and remix are not served. Each model accepts only the durations and sizes it publishes: a create naming anything else is refused 400 before anything is held. `GET /v1/models` lists the exact strings this key can call.

get.description: Read back the provider's current job object for a video job, for the account that created it. A terminal status seen here settles the job's money once; the read itself writes no usage row and is charged nothing. Charging reads the seconds the provider reports for the finished render, never the requested duration; where the provider reports none, the full hold is charged. External delivery URLs are omitted from the answer; download finished bytes through `GET /v1/videos/{id}/content`.

Error.description: The error envelope. One top-level `error` key, always, at every status.

message.description: Prose for a person. It may be reworded, so do not branch on it.

type.description: The category an SDK branches on. A closed set.

param.description: The request field at fault, or null. Present and null rather than absent.

code.description: The stable machine-readable reason. Branch on this.

request_id.description: Our id for this request, the same value as the x-hopscotch-request-id header. Quote it when you contact support.

ChatCompletionRequest.description: An OpenAI-compatible chat request. Accepted controls depend on the selected model and endpoint; a field listed here does not establish support for every model. Unsupported or unmetered features can be refused before a provider call.

model.description: The exact provider-qualified ID returned by GET /v1/models, for example vertex-ai/gemini-3.8-flash. The offering must include chat_completions in endpoint_families. A bare ID is refused with model_id_not_pinned. A profile/{identifier} value selects your routing profile instead.

messages.description: The conversation so far, in OpenAI message form.

stream.description: Return the reply as server-sent events instead of one JSON body.

max_tokens.description: The most output tokens you will accept. Sending it also lowers the credit held for the request while it runs, so it is the lever that keeps a request under your account spend rate cap. Omit it and the model's published maximum output is held instead.

stream_options.description: Set include_usage to request a final usage chunk. For Gemini, read token totals and modality details there, then GET /v1/usage/{id} for the settled charge.

modalities.description: Requested output modalities. For an offered Vertex Gemini image model, use ["text", "image"]. Support is model-specific. Audio output is refused on platform-paid chat requests.

image_size.description: The model-specific image resolution. The verified Vertex example uses 1K.

image_config.description: Image controls for Gemini chat generation. Availability depends on the model. This is separate from the Images API size parameter.

reasoning_effort.description: A model-specific reasoning control. Use a value the selected model supports; low was verified for the Vertex text examples.

safety_settings.description: Vertex Gemini per-category safety settings, forwarded with their thresholds unchanged; Google validates categories and thresholds. OFF disables a category's configurable filter; BLOCK_NONE still returns safety scores. Omit the field to keep Google's defaults. safetySettings is accepted as the same field: send one spelling, because different values under both names are refused with 400 before a provider call.

presence_penalty.description: On Vertex Gemini a non-null value, including zero, is forwarded unchanged and Google decides whether the selected model accepts it; null is left out. Other providers apply their own rules.

frequency_penalty.description: On Vertex Gemini a non-null value, including zero, is forwarded unchanged and Google decides whether the selected model accepts it; null is left out. Other providers apply their own rules.

ChatCompletion.description: An OpenAI chat completion, as the provider produced it.

images.description: Gemini image output, separate from text content. Check this array even when content is empty.

url.description: A data URL containing the generated image.

usage.description: Provider-normalized usage. For Vertex Gemini, prompt_tokens + completion_tokens + completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens equals total_tokens. Chat image tokens appear in completion_tokens_details.image_tokens when reported. Count modality subsets once.

TextCompletion.description: An OpenAI text completion, as the provider produced it.

Message.description: An Anthropic message, as the provider produced it.

UsageRecord.description: One request, as the key that made it can read it back.

request_id.description: The id the `x-hopscotch-request-id` header carried on the response this record is about.

occurred_at.description: When the request started, in RFC 3339.

model.description: The provider-qualified ID recorded for this request. A refusal before provider selection can prefix the requested full ID with unknown/; it does not mean an unknown provider served the request.

outcome.description: How the request ended, from a closed set of words. A request that was answered is `served`.

usage.description: Stored prompt, completion, total, cache and reasoning counters. Null means no count was recorded; zero is a recorded zero. This lookup does not currently return the audio/image modality splits carried by the original inference response.

cache_write_tokens.description: The cache write at the default lifetime. It does not include `cache_write_1h_tokens`, so add the two to read the whole write.

cache_write_1h_tokens.description: The one-hour part of the cache write. Null where the provider stated no split.

charge.description: What the request cost, with what you need to check it against the rates GET /v1/models publishes. Present only when your workspace balance paid for the request, so it is absent when `paid_from_allowance` is true.

amount_micros.description: The charge in millionths of one dollar, so 1000000 is $1.00. Null where the request was never priced, which is not the same as a charge of zero.

amount.description: The same figure as dollars a person reads, with up to six decimal places and trailing zeros trimmed. Null exactly when `amount_micros` is null.

rate_revision_id.description: An opaque identifier for the published rate revision associated with the charge. Preserve it with the request ID when checking a charge; context tier and effective date can select different rates within that pricing history.

note.description: What was unusual about this charge, or null on an ordinary one. `rate_absent_charged_at_anchor`: part of the request was priced at a rate the model does not list, a cache read or write at the input rate or reasoning at the output rate. `estimated_from_delivered_text`: the stream stopped before the provider reported its counts, so the charge is the prompt we counted plus an output estimated from the text delivered, never above the amount held. `exact_from_provider_frame`: the stream stopped early but the provider counts had already arrived, so the charge is exact.

served_on_own_key.description: True when the request ran on your own provider key, which is why nothing was charged. Read this rather than inferring it from a zero charge.

paid_from_allowance.description: True when an included allowance paid for the request, in which case `charge` is absent.

latency_ms.description: Total time the caller waited, in milliseconds.

note.description: A fixed sentence saying no prompt and no response body was stored.

created.description: A unix timestamp in seconds. The release time where one is recorded and the record's own creation time otherwise, so it is not a release date for most of the list.

shutdown_date.description: When the model stops serving, in unix seconds. Absent when there is none, rather than null.

CatalogCapabilities.description: What the catalog records this model can do. Each answer is one of three words, and `unknown` is not `no`: it means nobody has established the answer.

ModelExtension.description: Our own facts about a model, under the `uniblock` key, which keeps the platform's original name because it is protocol a deployed client reads. Everything OpenAI's own model object defines stays at the top level; everything it does not define lives here.

model_id.description: The model name without its provider prefix. Send the top-level id as model; it contains the provider-qualified value the API accepts.

author.description: Who made the model, which is not who serves it.

input_rate_thousandths.description: The published customer input price, in thousandths of the currency unit per million tokens. A model priced only per unit, such as an image, audio, or video model, omits token rate fields. Read the model offering for the current price; this field is not a provider-cost disclosure.

output_rate_thousandths.description: The same unit, for completion tokens. Absent when the model publishes no separate output rate or is priced only per unit.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217, or null where nobody recorded one.

endpoint_families.description: Published request families for this offering. Support on chat_completions does not establish support on image_generations or another endpoint.

provider_display_names.description: Who can serve it. Which one answered a given request is on the response headers, not here.

ModelParameter.description: One request parameter this model accepts. The three bounds are in thousandths of the parameter's own unit, so a temperature ceiling of 2 arrives as 2000 and a default of 0.7 as 700. Integers, because a bound that drifted in its last decimal place would be a contract about nothing.

type.description: The control shape a client should render.

sent_by_default.description: Whether a client sends this parameter unless it is told otherwise.

description.description: Detail only. The list is scanned and the detail is read, so the prose a model carries is served where somebody asked for that one model.

parameters.description: Recorded parameter controls. An empty array means no controls were recorded, not that the model accepts no optional parameters.

replacement_model_id.description: What to move to, where one is named.

supported_parameters.description: Recorded supported-parameter names, with disproved capabilities withheld. Null or an empty array means support metadata is unavailable or unrecorded, not that every unlisted parameter is rejected.

ModelDetail.description: One model, in the same envelope the list uses, with the detail-only fields under `uniblock`.

shutdown_date.description: Absent when the model has no announced end.
